evidence.C1: Journal uses 'No. 01' numbering and dotted ledger lines; tank art features depth haze and distinct species silhouettes.
evidence.C2: 'More to do' card clearly guides next steps, but mobile fishing screen crowds the viewport with 'Controls' and 'Bait' cards.
evidence.C3: Interlocking loops include nitrogen cycle, fishing minigame, greenhouse cuttings, reef lab genetics, and focus timer.
evidence.C4: Consistent pill buttons and layered shadows across screens; 'Care' modal tiles are neatly aligned.

fixes: Maximize the fishing gameplay viewport on mobile by collapsing the 'Controls' and 'Bait' cards into accordions or overlays, as they currently reduce the visible water area.
Group secondary tank actions (Shop, Photo, Watch, Share) into a 'More' menu or horizontal scroll row on mobile to reduce button density in the thumb zone.
Make the primary maintenance action (e.g., 'Change 40% of water') sticky or prominent at the top of the Care modal so it isn't pushed below the fold on smaller screens.

evidence.C1: Distinctive field-guide aesthetic with 'numbered plates I and II', 'No. 1' order entries, dotted ledger lines; tank drawn as glass box with perspective side panes, receding gravel floor, depth haze, back-glass planting silhouettes, fish floor shadows, lid rim, stand; stones and driftwood carry contact shadows, top-light highlight, core shadow, moss cap; koi pond has rim stones, lanterns, bamboo fountain, drifting maple/ginkgo leaves
evidence.C2: 'More to do' section explicitly guides first-time players with 'Go fishing', 'Greenhouse and reef lab', 'Field journal'; tools row clearly labelled (Feed, Care, Scape, Residents, Shop, Photo, Watch, Share); fishing scene shows 'Flick up on the water, or press Cast' with Flick/Classic toggle; phone layout shows tools in clean 2x4 grid with nothing cramped
evidence.C3: Interlocking loops clearly exceed typical cozy aquarium: nitrogen cycle care, 9-spot fishing with flick/reel/tension/drag mechanics, breeding with inherited colours, aquascaping (16 plants, 8 hardscape, 3 substrates, 3 tank sizes, reef room), greenhouse trays with variegated sports, reef lab with named strains from form/two colours/pattern, journal dex with silhouettes and hints, focus timer with box breathing, separate koi pond with generative sound mix
evidence.C4: Consistent pill buttons, floating white cards with layered shadows, warm cream palette with dark green accents maintained across all screens; feedback messages well-placed ('Tap a fish to meet it, or tap the glass', 'Line is slack. Reel.'); however some spacing in the desktop tank side column feels slightly loose and the koi pond's top-down style, while cohesive, breaks slightly from the field-guide motif

fixes: Refine fish art — while the tank environment is richly detailed (glass box perspective, depth haze, shadows), the fish themselves read as small and simple in both desktop and phone views; making each of the 47 species more visually distinctive would strengthen the 'tank art is the hero' goal

Tighten spacing and visual hierarchy in the desktop tank side column — the 'More to do', 'Water test', and 'Today's care' cards have generous gaps that make the right column feel less dense than the tank; grouping related items more tightly would improve scanability

Add more environmental detail to fishing spots — the lily pond scenery is pleasant but flatter than the main tank's layered glass-box art; matching the fishing scenes' depth (haze, foreground/midground/background layers) would unify the visual craft across screens

evidence.C1: Coherent cream/green palette and serif/sans pairing; tank rendered with 'perspective side panes, receding gravel floor, depth haze' plus visible light rays, distinct tetra forms and contact shadows; koi pond and field-guide journal plates ('No. 01', dotted ledger lines) are distinctive. Held from 9-10: fishing scenes are visibly flatter (plain gradient water, simple hill silhouettes, sparse pads) than the tank/pond art, so not 'every screen feels designed'.
evidence.C2: Strong next-step guidance: 'Tap a fish to meet it, or tap the glass.', 'Flick up on the water, or press Cast', 'Line is slack. Reel', 'Try Lily pond · fresh', 'Pick a length and start when you are ready.'; phone tools are a labelled 2x4 grid, nothing cramped. Held from 9-10: tank desktop stacks competing prompts - 'Test the water' appears in both the Water test card and Today's care checklist while 'More to do' adds three more calls to action.
evidence.C3: Every anchor loop present: nitrogen-cycle care, fishing minigame (tension vs strength, drag, 9 spots, tournaments, 47 species), breeding with inherited colours, scaping, greenhouse with variegated sports, reef lab strains, orders, journal, focus; loops interlock via 'arrow links to the next step of each loop (harvest a tray, trim plants in the tank, plant cuttings with Scape)'. Held from 10: depth of breeding/tournament/reef loops is asserted in the summary, not demonstrated - screenshots show early game (journal 3 of 47, Level 1/6).
evidence.C4: Consistent pill buttons, white cards, tiles and nav across all nine screenshots; feedback is unobtrusive and well placed ('Line is slack. Reel' pill over scene, quiet pond controls that fade). Held from 9-10: Garden hub is dense with many simultaneous modules, and journal card No. 03 carries a green top edge the sibling cards lack - a state whose meaning is not evident.

fixes: Raise the fishing scenes' art to the tank/koi-pond standard - richer water and shore composition instead of flat hills and plain gradient water (biggest C1 lever, w=0.30).

De-duplicate the Tank screen's prompts: merge the Water test card's 'Test the water' with the care checklist entry and trim 'More to do' so the next step reads as one clear action (biggest C2 lever, w=0.30).

Make the deeper loops visible in-product - breeding inheritance previews, tournament standings, reef strain lineage - and tighten the Garden hub's grouping/spacing so asserted depth and tidiness are demonstrable (C3/C4).
